info.title: HCML Monitoring Portal (BFF)
info.summary: A read-only backend-for-frontend over the Zabbix 7.0 JSON-RPC API.
info.description:
The portal owns no database. Every response below is either passed through from Zabbix or
derived in-process and cached in an LRU of at most 500 entries or about 64 MB, whichever is
reached first, that is lost on restart. Sites, links,
incidents, host reachability and the monthly SLA have no table anywhere.

**One write exists** in the whole surface: `POST /api/problems/acknowledge`. It uses a separate
write-capable Zabbix token and is refused with 503 when that token is unset.

### Authentication

One credential, a JWT carrying `{ sub, role, ep }` that lasts 12 hours unless `SESSION_HOURS` sets another
length (2 to 24), presented one of two ways.
Every guarded path takes either:

- `sessionCookie`, the browser's way. `POST /api/auth/login` and `POST /api/auth/refresh` set it
  with `Set-Cookie`: `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`, `Path=/`, a `Max-Age` equal to the session length
  (43200 at the default 12 hours), and `Secure` when
  the request arrived over HTTPS. No script on the page can read it, and no response body carries
  the token. An open portal renews it with `POST /api/auth/refresh` an hour before it runs out;
  `POST /api/auth/logout` clears it.
- `bearerAuth`, `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>`, for scripts and tests. A script takes the token
  from the login response's `Set-Cookie` header. When a request carries both, the header wins.

No path takes a token in the query string, `/api/stream` included: `EventSource` sends the cookie
like any same-origin request, so a `?token=` gets 401. `logging.ts` and nginx still redact one
from their logs, for pages loaded before the cookie change.

**Forgery check.** A `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` or `DELETE` on `/api/*` that authenticates with the
cookie, and every call to `POST /api/auth/login` and `POST /api/auth/logout`, must carry the
header `X-HCML-CSRF: 1`. When the browser sends an `Origin`, it must name the request's own host
and port. Anything else gets `403 csrf` (`CsrfRefused`), before the guard runs and with auth on
or off. A request with a Bearer header is not checked, except on sign-in and sign-out, since a browser
never adds one by itself.
`csrfRefusal` in `auth.ts:117-127`; ADR-0010.

The guard judges the route the router matched, not the URL text, so a percent-encoded path such
as `/%61pi/hosts` is guarded like `/api/hosts`. Only `/api/health`, `/api/auth/login`,
`/api/auth/me` and `/api/auth/logout` are outside it, matched exactly.

When `AUTH_ENABLED=false` no route is guarded at all and every caller is treated as `admin`. The
forgery check still applies to sign-in and sign-out.

### Roles

OpenAPI cannot express a role requirement per path, so each operation states its role in the
description. From `ROUTE_RULES` (`server/src/security/auth.ts:39-44`), first match wins, unmatched is
`viewer`:

| Role | Paths |
|---|---|
| `admin` | `/api/reports/inventory` |
| `operator` | `/api/links`, `/api/net/*`, `POST /api/problems/acknowledge` |
| `viewer` | everything else |

### Errors

Every error, at every status, is `{ "error": string, "message": string, "requestId": string }`. There
is no `statusCode` in the body and no other field. `requestId` is the reply's `X-Request-Id` (see
Request ids below), so a person who reads it out lets an admin find the request in the logs.

### Request ids

Every reply, at every status and on the live stream too, carries an `X-Request-Id` header. nginx makes
the id for each request (`$request_id`, 32 hex characters), replacing any value the client sent, and
the BFF uses it: it is `reqId` on every BFF log line of the request, the header on the reply, and
`requestId` in the body of an error. nginx writes it in its own access log as `rid=`. A request that
reaches the BFF some other way keeps a sent id only when it is 8 to 64 characters of letters, digits,
`.`, `_` and `-`, and gets a new one otherwise.

Two pairs are easy to conflate and are deliberately different:

- A rejected portal JWT is `401 unauthorized`. A rejected Zabbix API token is
  `503 zabbix_auth`. Different tokens, different codes.
- An unreachable or erroring Zabbix is `502 zabbix_error`; a Zabbix that does not answer within
  `ZABBIX_TIMEOUT_MS` is `503 zabbix_timeout`. **Nothing in this server ever returns 504.**

### Sign-in off

With `AUTH_ENABLED=false` (local development only) every caller is admin, so the server answers
only to a `Host` header that names this machine: `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `::1` or the
`WEB_ORIGIN` host, on any port. Any other `Host` gets `421 misdirected_request`, which stops a
page on another site that points its own domain at 127.0.0.1 (DNS rebinding). With sign-in on
this does nothing, a token is checked instead.

### Compression

JSON responses of 1024 bytes or more are compressed with brotli (quality 4) or gzip (level 6);
brotli wins ties. `Vary: Accept-Encoding` is set on every eligible JSON response whether or not
compression actually happened. The two SSE paths bypass the hook entirely.

### Stale answers

The slow reports are served with `staleIfError`: `/api/reports/availability`,
`/api/reports/noise`, `/api/reports/capacity`, and the derived monthly SLA behind `/api/sli`,
`/api/sli/export`, `/api/services/derived` and `/api/explain/sla` with `source=derived`. When
Zabbix fails they return **200 with an old copy, of any age**, rather than 502/503. The status code
does not say so, but two response headers do:

- `X-Data-Stale: true`
- `X-Data-Age-Seconds: <how old the copy is, in seconds>`

They appear only on an answer that read an old copy kept because Zabbix failed, never on a live
answer, a cache hit or an error, and the JSON body is not changed. When one request read several
cached reports, the age is that of the oldest. A cached answer that was itself built on a stale
report, `/api/services/derived` for its 30 s and `/api/explain/sla`, is not flagged again.

get.summary: Liveness, build and readiness
get.description:
Unguarded and not rate limited, like `POST /api/auth/logout`. Registered before the auth guard
(`index.ts:76`) and in the rate limiter's allow-list, so it answers even when Zabbix is down.
The status stays 200 then too: `ok` means the process answers, and `ready` says whether Zabbix
does.

`ready` comes from one `host.get` (`output: hostid`, `limit: 1`) with the read-only token, given
up after 2 s, one at a time, and kept for 15 s. A result 15 to 60 s old is returned at once while
a new check runs behind it; an older one makes the caller wait. For a local model the same check
reads `GET {AI_BASE_URL}/models` once, with the model key when one is set. The hosted Anthropic model
is not probed, and the model never changes `ready.ok`. `apiinfo.version` is not used: Zabbix refuses it
when called with a token, and the Zabbix version is not worth publishing here.

`writeBack` tells the UI whether to render the acknowledge and close buttons.

The route is public, so anyone gets the liveness fields (`ok`, `ts`, `ai`, `aiProvider`,
`aiExternal`, `writeBack`, `defaults`) and none of them holds a URL, host name, token or error
text. A caller who is signed in, by cookie or Bearer header, also gets `version`, `startedAt`,
`build`, `ready` and `streams`: an anonymous caller must not learn the build, when the portal
restarted, how many screens are open, or that the Zabbix token was revoked. A bad or missing
token is never a 401 here, it just gets the short answer, and the readiness check is only
read for a signed-in caller. With sign-in off every caller counts as signed in. The container
healthcheck sends no sign-in and reads only the status.

ai.description: Whether the plain-language layer is configured.

aiProvider.description: Which backend answers, `AI_PROVIDER`. The page uses it to name the service in the notice below.

aiExternal.description:
Whether a question leaves this machine: true only when the hosted Anthropic backend is configured. The
Assistant and Explain then say so next to every answer; a local model shows nothing.

writeBack.description: Whether write-back is on, which is `ZABBIX_WRITE_TOKEN` set and either sign-in on or `ALLOW_WRITE_WITHOUT_AUTH=true`. False means acknowledge returns 503.

timezone.description: The SLA time zone, `SLA_TIMEZONE`. The web app labels times and cuts its month lists in it.

version.description: Signed-in callers only. The server package version.

startedAt.description: Signed-in callers only. When this process started.

build.description:
Signed-in callers only. The image's `BUILD_COMMIT` and `BUILD_TIME` build arguments (compose's `build.args`).
`unknown` when not given or empty, and cut to 64 characters.

ok.description: The portal can read Zabbix. The model never changes it.

zabbixMs.description: How long the Zabbix call took. Null when it did not answer.

model.description: `off` is no model configured, `not_checked` is the hosted Anthropic model, which a probe would bill.

checkedAt.description: When these answers were read, milliseconds since epoch.

streams.description: Signed-in callers only. Screens connected to `/api/stream` right now.

get.summary: Whether the portal can read Zabbix, as a status code
get.description:
For a monitor that holds a session cookie or a Bearer token, so it is guarded like any route and
needs `viewer`. `GET /api/health` always answers 200 and says inside `ready` whether Zabbix does;
this answers `503` while the portal cannot read Zabbix, so a status check is enough.

It reads the same cached check as `/api/health`: one `host.get` with the read-only token, given up
after 2 s, one at a time, kept for 15 s. Asking both, or asking often, costs Zabbix at most one call
in 15 s. The model never changes the status: the AI layer is optional, and `model` only reports it.

The body is the same at both statuses: the check's own fields, as `ready` carries them in
`/api/health`, and the version, start time, build and screens a signed-in `/api/health` carries.
It holds no address, token or error text. The status says whether to worry, `zabbix` says why.

200.description: Zabbix answered the read-only token's call.

503.description: The portal cannot read Zabbix. `zabbix` says why (`token_rejected`, `timeout` or `error`).

post.summary: Exchange credentials for a session cookie
post.description:
Registered before the guard, so it is reachable unauthenticated. Rate-limited twice,
deliberately, since it is otherwise an unthrottled password oracle: the global limit, and 10
attempts a minute per account and address of its own (`LOGIN_ATTEMPTS_PER_MINUTE` in `auth.ts`).
After 10 failures in a row for one account from one address, sign-in is locked for a minute,
doubling with each further failure up to 5 minutes; a success clears it. Both answer 429 with
`Retry-After`.

Credentials come from `PORTAL_USERS` (comma-separated `name:password:role` triples) or from
`PORTAL_USER`/`PORTAL_PASS` as a single-admin shorthand. A password is plain text or an scrypt
hash (`scrypt.N.r.p.salt.hash`, made by `server/scripts/hash-password.ts`), and either is compared
in constant time. A plain one is still plain text in the environment.

The token goes into the session cookie, never the body. Needs `X-HCML-CSRF: 1`, with or
without a cookie, and with auth off too: a refused sign-in gets 403 and sets no cookie.

The body must be a JSON object with a text `username` and a text `password`. One that is not,
for example a missing field or a number, is a 400 `bad_request`, not a 401, and does not count
as a failed sign-in. Empty text is still a wrong password: 401. Other fields are ignored.

200.description: Signed in. The session cookie is set.

401.description: `invalid_credentials`, no user has that name and password.

413.description: `fst_err_ctp_body_too_large`: a sign-in body over 4 KB (`LOGIN_BODY_LIMIT` in `auth.ts`).

get.summary: Who the current session says you are, and how long it has left
get.description:
Self-verifying: registered before the guard and calls `jwtVerify()` itself, on the cookie or
a Bearer header. Drives the sidebar's role filter, which is cosmetic: the BFF enforces with a
403 regardless. `pages` gives the role each menu page needs, worked out from the guard's own
rules (`pageAccess.ts`), so the sidebar keeps no second copy of them. `expiresIn` is relative,
so the page times its renewal without trusting its own clock.

When `AUTH_ENABLED=false` this returns `{ authEnabled: false, user: { name: "anonymous",
role: "admin" }, expiresIn: null, pages }`. `user` is **never** null, despite `web/src/types.ts`
allowing it.

expiresIn.description: Seconds until the session ends. Null with auth off.

pages.description: The minimum role for each menu page, by path, such as `/network`.

post.summary: Swap a valid session for a fresh one
post.description:
Keeps an open portal signed in, for every user, for as long as the page stays open
(DESIGN.md section 9, "Wall sign-in"; ADR-0009). The web app calls it an hour before the
session ends, timed from the `expiresIn` of the last sign-in, renewal or `GET /api/auth/me`.
A closed tab renews nothing.

Behind the guard, so it takes the cookie or a Bearer header; a `?token=` is refused like on
every route. A cookie renewal is a cookie POST and needs `X-HCML-CSRF: 1`; a Bearer renewal
does not. The user is looked up again in the current user list: one removed from
`PORTAL_USERS`, or a name listed there twice, gets 401 and no cookie, and the new token carries
the role configured now, not the one in the old token. It takes no body: none, or a JSON
object that is ignored. Any other JSON body is a 400. Registered only when
`AUTH_ENABLED=true`; otherwise 404.

requestBody.description: Ignored. Nothing, or a JSON object.

200.description: Renewed. The session cookie is set again with a fresh token.

post.summary: Sign out by clearing the session cookie
post.description:
Public, so a missing or expired cookie can still be cleared: answers 200 with or without one,
and with auth off. The `Set-Cookie` header empties the cookie with the attributes it was set
with. It clears the cookie in this browser only: the BFF keeps no list to cancel tokens on, so a
copied token keeps working until it expires, up to `SESSION_HOURS` (12 by default). Taking the user
out of `PORTAL_USERS` and restarting the BFF ends their access at once; a new `JWT_SECRET`, or a
higher `SESSION_EPOCH` and a restart, ends every session at once (SC-14). A live stream opened before then is ended when its token expires, and the browser reconnects (SC-15). Needs `X-HCML-CSRF: 1` like any POST that touches the cookie. It takes no body: none, or a JSON object that is ignored. Any other JSON body is a 400.

requestBody.description: Ignored. Nothing, or a JSON object.

200.description: Signed out. The session cookie is cleared.

Set-Cookie.description:
The session cookie, emptied: `Max-Age=0` and an `Expires` in 1970, with the same
`Path`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite` and `Secure` it was set with.

get.summary: Every monitored host, with its resolved site
get.description:
Cached 30 s. `site` is derived by `naming.ts` from four ranked signals: tag, host name,
inventory, group, because no HCML host carries a site tag. It is null when none match.

get.summary: Hosts with reachability state and problem counts
get.description:
Cached 15 s. `state` is the portal's own reachability judgement (`reachability.ts`), ping
first, interface flags only as a fallback, on 17 Sep, 16 of 23 hosts Zabbix called
unavailable answered ping. `reason` records which signal decided it.

get.summary: Every host as a device of one kind, for the Devices page
get.description:
Cached 30 s. The same hosts, reachability and problem counts as `/api/hosts/overview`, which it
reads through the same cache entry, each with the kind of device it is and the monitoring
template that decided it. The kind is the one the derived SLA report uses (`naming.ts`
`deviceClass`: the template first, then the name), so the two count a switch the same way. The
templates are read once for five minutes. A host whose templates have not been read yet comes
back with category `Other`. `classes` lists every kind in the order the page shows them, with
its plural name.

get.summary: Zabbix host groups
get.description: Straight `hostgroup.get` passthrough. Cached 60 s. 23 groups in HCML's estate.

get.summary: Items for a host, or by explicit ids
get.description:
Cached 30 s. `hostid` is required unless `itemids` is given.

`search` is passed to Zabbix with `startSearch: true` deliberately: without it Zabbix runs
`LIKE '%…%'` and scans all 51,845 items at about 105 ms per call.

parameters.name: hostid
parameters.description: Required unless `itemids` is supplied. Numeric.

parameters.name: itemids
parameters.description: Comma-separated numeric ids, de-duplicated. At most 50 or 400.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Prefix match on `key_`.

parameters.name: graphable
parameters.description: Numeric items only. Truthy for exactly `1` or `true`; anything else is false.

get.summary: Latest values, paged or capped
get.description:
Cached 15 s. **The presence of `page` switches mode**, and the two modes differ in more than
pagination: paged mode searches `name` OR `key_`, un-paged searches `name` only.

With neither `hostid` nor `groupid` this returns an empty result with 200, not 400.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Presence switches to paged mode.

200.description:
`total`, `page` and `pageSize` are present only in paged mode. `truncated` means the cap
was hit: 500 rows un-paged, 20,000 ids paged.

get.summary: Open problems
get.description:
Cached 5 s, and never served stale: an operator who has just acknowledged must not be
shown the previous list. About 664 problems at HCML, 459 kB compressing to 25 kB.

The list also carries problems Zabbix resolved moments ago (`r_eventid` other than `0`),
which the Problems page marks Resolved, and problems raised inside a planned maintenance
window (`suppressed` = `1`), marked In maintenance. The Dashboard and every server-side
count (`/api/stats`, sites, the hosts overview, maps, aging, the services tree, the
Assistant's snapshot) leave both out, as Zabbix's own dashboard does.

get.summary: Live problem stream (SSE)
get.description:
`text/event-stream`. **Exempt from the rate limit, but capped:** at most `STREAM_MAX_CLIENTS`
(default 100) screens in all and `STREAM_MAX_PER_USER` (default 5) for one signed-in user, or for
one client address with auth off. A screen past either limit gets `429 too_many_streams` with
`Retry-After: 30`, before any stream header. The browser's `EventSource` cannot read that body,
so it falls back to polling and retries.

One shared 5 s ticker serves every client. A frame is sent at once when the fingerprint over
`eventid:severity:acknowledged:suppressed:r_eventid` changes. A list identical to the last one
sent is never sent again, and one where only a name or host changed goes after at most 30 s. A change in tags alone is not in the frame. A
new client receives the current frame immediately, and an acknowledge force-pushes one.

Three frame kinds:

| Frame | Payload |
|---|---|
| `event: problems` | the problems of `GET /api/problems`, cut to the fields the Dashboard reads: `eventid`, `objectid`, `object`, `name`, `severity`, `clock`, `r_eventid`, `acknowledged`, `suppressed`, `host` and `hostid`. No tags, `opdata`, `r_clock`, `manualClose` or other field Zabbix returns (about half the size of the full list) |
| `event: error` | `{ "message": string }` |
| `event: ping` | after 15 s with nothing else sent, so a client can tell a quiet line from a dead one: `{ "ageMs": n }`, the age of the last good read of the list, when known, and `{}` otherwise |

A client that sends `Accept-Encoding: gzip` (every browser does) gets the stream gzip-compressed,
flushed after every frame and keep-alive, with `Content-Encoding: gzip` and `Vary: Accept-Encoding`;
on HCML's list the first frame goes from 166 kB to 19 kB.

The stream ends when the session token it was opened with expires, so the browser reconnects
with the renewed cookie or is sent to sign in, and when the BFF shuts down on `SIGTERM`.

No `id:` field is emitted, so `Last-Event-ID` resumption is not supported. Browsers cannot
set headers on `EventSource`, but it sends the session cookie on a same-origin request like
any other, so the stream authenticates by cookie. A `?token=` is refused with 401 here as on
every route.

200.description: The stream opens and stays open until its token expires.

429.description: `too_many_streams`, the portal or this account is at its screen limit.

get.summary: Downsampled series for up to four items
get.description:
Cached 15 s live, 600 s historical. **Three mutually exclusive range modes, in precedence
order: `month`, then `from`+`to`, then `hours`.**

Below 24 hours it reads raw history; above, hourly trends; and `source` in the response says
which was used. Everything is bucketed to at most `points` per series, so a 30-day graph is a
few tens of kB rather than 500. An explicit `null` point is inserted wherever the gap between
samples exceeds 3× the expected spacing, so the chart breaks the line instead of drawing
across a collection gap.

parameters.name: itemids
parameters.description: Comma-separated. At most 4 or 400.

parameters.name: month
parameters.description: Highest precedence. A future month is 400.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Unix seconds. Must be paired with `to`. Range may not exceed 400 days, as asked.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Unix seconds. The range is widened to whole minutes (`from` down, `to` up), and the response says the range it used, so requests seconds apart share one cached read.

parameters.name: hours
parameters.description: Used only when neither `month` nor `from`/`to` is given.

parameters.name: points
parameters.description: Target samples per series after bucketing.

400.description: Bad range, more than 4 items, unknown itemids, or a non-numeric item.

403.description: `forbidden`, a viewer asked for a network interface item (key starting `net.if`). Operators and admins may read them.

get.summary: Network devices with ICMP state
get.description: **operator.** Cached 30 s. Narrowed to `NET_GROUP_IDS` when that is configured.

get.summary: Internet traffic meters, read from the gauge widgets of a Zabbix dashboard
get.description:
**operator.** Cached 30 s. The dashboard itself is kept for two minutes.

Reads the dashboard named by `INTERNET_METERS_DASHBOARD` (default `Global view`, HCML's own) with
`dashboard.get` and makes one meter of each gauge widget: the interface item it is bound to, the
capacity it was given as its maximum, and its colour zones. The meters come in the order a person
reads the pages, and a later page that repeats an item adds nothing. Nothing is created or changed
in Zabbix.

The value is the item's last value. Zabbix keeps that only for a day, so an item with none (silent
for longer, or collected by a copy of Zabbix that has stopped) is read from history, one newest
row each, and comes back as `stale` with its own time. A reading counts as current for three
update intervals, and at least ten minutes. When no dashboard of that name is visible to the
Zabbix token, `found` is false and `meters` is empty.

Two more things are read for each gauge, from the items beside its own on the same host and the same
interface (the same ifIndex): the interface's status item, and the item of the opposite direction.
They are searched for once in two minutes (`item.get` by key prefix) and their values asked for with
the gauge's own. Only a current value counts, and none is ever read from history: a status or a
traffic figure from days ago says nothing about the link today. `link` says whether the interface is
up or down, and `other` is the opposite direction on the gauge's own scale and zones, which assumes a
link that is the same size both ways.

get.summary: Interfaces for one device, searched then filtered then paged
get.description:
**operator.** Cached 15 s.

Order matters and is observable: `search` is applied first, `summary` is computed over the
searched set, *then* `status` filters, *then* the page is sliced. So `summary` counts more
rows than `rows` contains whenever `status` is set.

**`status` fails silently.** Any value outside the enum is treated as no filter rather than
rejected with 400.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring of `name` or `alias`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: An unrecognised value is ignored, not rejected.

get.summary: The busiest hosts right now, by CPU and by memory
get.description:
Cached 30 s. For each of CPU and memory, the hosts with the highest current utilisation, as the
Zabbix dashboard widget "Top hosts" lists them. The items are found by key prefix and by the same rules
as the capacity report (`system.cpu.util`, `vm.memory.util`, the SNMP forms of Cisco and FortiGate), so
the idle share is never taken. A host with several matching items counts once, by its hottest.

Only a current value is listed: an item whose last value is older than three of its intervals (and at
least ten minutes) is counted in `considered` and not in `current`, and is never read from history, so
a copy of Zabbix that has stopped gives `current: 0` and no rows.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows for each metric.

get.summary: Web scenarios that pass, fail or have no current result
get.description:
Cached 30 s. Every enabled web scenario of a monitored host is counted once, as the Zabbix dashboard widget
"Web monitoring" counts them, from the item that holds its result (`web.test.fail[<scenario>]`: 0 when every
step passed, otherwise the step that failed).

Only a current result is believed: one older than three of the item's intervals (and at least ten minutes),
an item Zabbix cannot collect and an item that has collected nothing are `unknown`, so a scenario nobody has
run lately is never read as OK. The failed ones are listed by host and then by name, as many as `limit` says,
and `failed` counts them all.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Failed scenarios to list.

200.description: The counts and the failed scenarios.

get.summary: The triggers that fired most often
get.description:
Cached 60 s. Reads at most 10,000 events and returns the top 100; `truncated` says the cap
was hit, which it will be for large `days`.

get.summary: Estate counts for the dashboard tiles
get.description:
Cached 30 s. Four count-only Zabbix calls in parallel plus the shared problem list. `hosts`
counts enabled (monitored) hosts only, as the Dashboard's card says, and `items` counts
monitored items.

get.summary: When Zabbix last collected a value
get.description:
Whether Zabbix is still collecting, for the Dashboard. A stopped `zabbix-server` leaves every
API call working and every value in place, so the newest `lastclock` of any supported ICMP item
is the only sign. It is rolled up from the same `item.get` the host states read, so asking for
both costs Zabbix one call.

The newest clock is cached 30 s; `ageSeconds` is worked out at each request. `stale` is true
once nothing has been collected for `staleAfterSeconds`, ten minutes (the floor `isFresh` allows
before it stops believing a ping), and is never true while the age is unknown, which happens
when no ICMP item exists. A Zabbix failure is an error, not an invented age.

lastCollectedAt.description: When Zabbix last collected a value, Unix seconds. Null when there is no ICMP item to tell.

pinged.description: Hosts whose latest ping is fresh.

answering.description: How many of those answered it.

reachLost.description:
At least 10 hosts were pinged and at most a fifth of them answered, so Zabbix has more
likely lost its way into the network than every device its power.

get.summary: Open problems per host group
get.description: Cached 15 s. Groups with no problems are omitted; the rest are sorted descending.

200.description: Groups carrying at least one problem.

get.summary: Per-host availability over a window
get.description:
Cached 120 s with `staleIfError`: an upstream failure returns 200 with an old copy, marked
by `X-Data-Stale` and `X-Data-Age-Seconds` (see Stale answers above).

**Two bases with materially different responses.** With `basis=availability` (the default)
the derived SLI engine runs and `overall`, `categories`, `sites`, `target`, `profile` and
`gaps` are all present. With `basis=all-problems` none of them are, and each host carries
only its id, name, availability, downtime, incidents and longest outage.

`month` takes precedence over `days`. A month that has not started is 400, and so is one
more than 400 days ago, Zabbix keeps events about a year.

`basis=all-problems` counts a problem that began before the window and was still open when it
started from the window's first second, as the SLA engine does. Problems still open now are found
at any age, and so is one that began more than 31 days before the window and ended inside it: it is
found from its recovery event (BK-04). One that began more than 31 days before the window and
ended after it is missed. At most 200 such older outages are looked up one by one; past that,
`truncated` is true and the figures are a floor.

parameters.name: severity
parameters.description: Minimum severity. Defaults to `AVAILABILITY_MIN_SEVERITY`, normally 2.

parameters.name: month
parameters.description: Takes precedence over `days`.

parameters.name: profile
parameters.description: Ignored when `basis=all-problems`.

get.summary: Flapping, chronic and unactioned triggers
get.description:
Cached 120 s with `staleIfError`. Note `severity` defaults to 0 here, not 2 as on the
availability report. `top` cuts the returned list only: every aggregate above it covers all
triggers, and `total` says how many there were.

A problem that began before the window and was still open when it started is counted from the
window's first second, with its real start kept for its age, so a problem open for weeks can be
flagged chronic. The lookback is the same as for the availability report: still-open problems at
any age, resolved ones within 31 days before the window, and older ones that ended inside the window,
found from their recovery event (BK-04). `truncated` is true when more than 200 of those older outages
needed a lookup: the rest are left out and the figures are a floor.

get.summary: How long unacknowledged problems have been open
get.description:
Cached 15 s. `buckets` is always exactly four, labelled `Under 1h`, `1–4h`, `4–24h`,
`Over 24h`.

get.summary: Average and peak utilisation per item
get.description:
Cached 300 s with `staleIfError`, marked by `X-Data-Stale` when an old copy is served. **The
heaviest endpoint in the portal.** At `days=365` it
issues roughly 112 Zabbix calls, because `trend.get` is sliced to keep Zabbix's PHP within
its memory limit, and each call costs about 20 SQL statements upstream, 10,771 in total,
measured 22 Sep.

`avg` is the unweighted mean of the hourly averages, not a sample-weighted mean.

get.summary: Naming, site, owner and criticality completeness
get.description:
**admin: the only admin-gated path.** Cached 60 s, and the cheapest heavy report: exactly
one Zabbix call, everything else computed in process.

`dimensions` always has four entries in the order `naming`, `site`, `owner`, `criticality`.
`scored: false` means the deployment has not configured that check.

get.summary: WAN links and paths, from ICMP item triplets
get.description:
**operator.** Cached 20 s.

A "link" is not a Zabbix entity. It is synthesised from the `icmpping`, `icmppingloss` and
`icmppingsec` items on a host, paired into a path by the `link_group` item tag. `jitter` is
max minus min RTT and appears only where min/max-mode items exist. The portal never speaks
ICMP itself, Zabbix polls, this reads the items.

get.summary: Hosts grouped into sites
get.description:
Cached 15 s. Zabbix has no site entity. `naming.ts` resolves one from four ranked
signals, tag, host name, inventory, group, and `coverage` reports how many hosts each
signal accounted for, which is the metric for the standardisation goal.

get.summary: Zabbix-native service tree
get.description:
Cached 30 s. Recursive, depth-capped at 12, and de-duplicated by `serviceid` because a shared
dependency legitimately appears under two parents: it is a DAG, not a tree.

**At HCML this returns an empty tree**: the `services` table has zero rows. Use
`/api/sla/source` to decide whether to render this or the derived equivalent.

get.summary: The portal's own service tree
get.description:
Cached 30 s. Deliberately emits the same shape as `/api/services` plus extra fields, so one
component renders either. Builds root → business services → sites → device class → hosts,
each node carrying the derived monthly SLA for its subtree. The monthly report under it can be
an old copy when Zabbix fails, in which case the answer carries `X-Data-Stale`.

get.summary: Whether Zabbix's own SLA has anything in it
get.description:
Cached 60 s. `real: false` tells the UI to switch to the derived SLA. **At HCML it is always
false**: one placeholder SLA object, no services, nothing attached.

get.summary: Zabbix SLA definitions
get.description: Cached 60 s.

get.summary: Zabbix-computed SLI per service
get.description:
Cached 60 s.

Both ids are checked before the cache key is built, so a junk value is a 400 and never a Zabbix
error. **Inconsistency:** omitting `slaid` still returns `[]` with 200, whereas
`/api/explain/sla` rejects the same omission with 400.

parameters.name: slaid
parameters.description: A numeric id. Missing gives an empty array and 200.

get.summary: The portal's derived monthly SLA
get.description:
Cached 24 h for a closed month, 5 min for the current one, both with `staleIfError`: when
Zabbix fails the old report is served with `X-Data-Stale: true` and `X-Data-Age-Seconds`. The
cache key carries the closed flag, so a figure computed mid-month is never kept as that
month's final answer, and a closed month is pinned, so a flood of graph keys cannot push it out
of the cache.

Two profiles. `hcml-report` reproduces HCML's own published Availability Report and is
validated against it to the digit, 99.3796 % for June 2026, 99.7167 % July, 99.2313 %
August, 138 of 138 hosts within 60 seconds. `availability` is the stricter figure, and costs
roughly 20 Zabbix calls against the report profile's 6 because it also checks per-hour
collection coverage from trends.

parameters.name: month
parameters.description: Defaults to the current month in `Asia/Jakarta`.

get.summary: The monthly SLA report as a PDF or Excel download
get.description:
**viewer.** The figures `/api/sli` shows for one month, both methods side by side, as one
file. `format=pdf` is the printable report; `format=xlsx` is the workbook, a Summary sheet and
one sheet per table. The file states when it was generated and, for the current month, that its
figures are not final.

It reads the same cached reports as `/api/sli`, so a month the page has already loaded costs
no further Zabbix call, and it inherits that route's `staleIfError`: while Zabbix is failing it
can answer 200 with a file built from older figures, not 502, and says so with
`X-Data-Stale` and `X-Data-Age-Seconds`. Nothing is kept for long: a
built file is reused for ten seconds, then built again from the cached figures.

`format` is checked before Zabbix is asked, so a bad request costs nothing. `month` and
`format` are the only parameters: any other is a 400, so a misspelt `month` is never read as
the current month. `month` is
validated as on `/api/sli`, and a month that has not started, or is more than about 400 days
back, is a 400. The file name is made from the validated month alone, `HCML_SLA_Report_<month>.<format>`,
never from other request text.

The body is not JSON, so it is never compressed whatever `Accept-Encoding` says, and
`Cache-Control: private, no-store` keeps a shared cache from holding on to it.

parameters.name: month
parameters.description: Defaults to the current month in `Asia/Jakarta`. An empty value means the default.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Exactly `pdf` or `xlsx`, in lower case. Missing, anything else, or given twice is a 400.

Content-Disposition.description:
`attachment; filename="HCML_SLA_Report_2026-08.pdf"; filename*=UTF-8''HCML_SLA_Report_2026-08.pdf`.
Only letters, digits, underscore, hyphen and the dot of the extension can appear in it.

Content-Length.description: The size of the file in bytes.

get.summary: Zabbix maps
get.description: Cached 60 s.

get.summary: One map with its elements resolved
get.description:
Cached 30 s. **Returns an array, not a single object**: the maps `map.get` found for `mapid`, which
is one. Each has the map's own fields, its `links`, and its `selements`, the elements drawn on it.
Each element is the raw Zabbix element with a macro-expanded `labelText` and, for a host element, also
`hostid`, `hostName`, `problems` and `maxSeverity`.

The shape is open by construction: the handler spreads whatever Zabbix returns.

get.summary: Plain-language explanation of one problem
get.description:
Cached 1 h, keyed by the event id together with its acknowledged and resolved state, so
an explanation is not reused after the problem changes.

Buffered JSON, not streamed. This path sends the host name, trigger name, opdata, severity,
start time, flags and the problem's tags to the model: in `hcml-portal` that means they
leave the machine.

404.description: `not_found`, no open problem with that event id.

429.description:
`rate_limited`, more calls than the per-user limit a minute (`AI_CHAT_PER_MINUTE` and `AI_EXPLAIN_PER_MINUTE`, 10 each by default), or `ai_budget`, the daily token budget is used
up (hosted model only; `AI_DAILY_TOKENS_PER_USER` and `AI_DAILY_TOKENS_TOTAL`). `Retry-After` says how long to wait.

get.summary: Plain-language explanation of an SLA figure
get.description:
Cached 300 s. **Two mutually exclusive modes.**

With `source=derived` it explains the portal's own monthly figure and takes `month`,
`profile` and `scope`, where scope is `overall`, `site:<code>` or `category:<NAME>`; an
unmatched scope is 404. Otherwise it explains a Zabbix-native SLA and requires `slaid`.

`noData: true` marks an answer produced without calling the model because there was
nothing to measure.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: `derived` selects the portal's figure. Any other value selects Zabbix's.

parameters.name: slaid
parameters.description: Required when `source` is not `derived`.

429.description:
`rate_limited`, more calls than the per-user limit a minute (`AI_CHAT_PER_MINUTE` and `AI_EXPLAIN_PER_MINUTE`, 10 each by default), or `ai_budget`, the daily token budget is used
up (hosted model only; `AI_DAILY_TOKENS_PER_USER` and `AI_DAILY_TOKENS_TOTAL`). `Retry-After` says how long to wait.

get.summary: Ask the model backend to load
get.description:
Fire and forget. Returns 202 immediately and does the work detached: the only 202 in
the API.

On the hosted provider this is a no-op, so the warm-up costs nothing; on a local model it
loads the weights so the first real question is not paying for a cold start.

post.description:
`text/event-stream`, streamed token by token, never cached.

The request body is normalised rather than strictly validated: blank turns are dropped, each
turn is silently truncated at 2,000 characters, and the oldest turns are dropped until the
whole history fits a 3,000-character budget. What *is* rejected with 400: a non-array or
empty `messages`, a bad `role`, a non-string `content`, or a conversation not ending in a
user turn.

Four event names:

| Event | Payload |
|---|---|
| `context` | the estate snapshot's metadata, counts and a `truncated` flag |
| `token` | `{ "t": string }`, concatenate in order |
| `done` | `{ ms, text, firstTokenMs }`, `text` is the cleaned answer and replaces the concatenated tokens |
| `error` | `{ "message": string }` |

Once the response is hijacked the HTTP status can no longer change, so failures after that
point arrive as an `error` frame on a 200. Its message is fixed wording, as on `AiError`.

The snapshot and the focused-site block are sent between `~~~ BEGIN` and `~~~ END` lines and
the system prompt says they are data. Host, site, problem and service names in them are cut to
one line, with control characters removed, and capped at 80 characters (hosts and sites) or 200
(problems, services and SLAs), so text typed into a device cannot pose as an instruction.

429.description:
`rate_limited`, more calls than the per-user limit a minute (`AI_CHAT_PER_MINUTE` and `AI_EXPLAIN_PER_MINUTE`, 10 each by default), or `ai_budget`, the daily token budget is used
up (hosted model only; `AI_DAILY_TOKENS_PER_USER` and `AI_DAILY_TOKENS_TOTAL`). `Retry-After` says how long to wait.

post.description:
**operator. The only write in the entire portal.**

Four independent gates: a separate `ZABBIX_WRITE_TOKEN` (the read token can never write),
the operator role, a 503 when the write token is unset, and a 503 when sign-in is off, unless
the dev opt-in `ALLOW_WRITE_WITHOUT_AUTH=true` is set (with sign-in off every caller is admin). `GET /api/health` exposes
`writeBack` so the UI can hide the buttons rather than offer a call that will fail.

Closing additionally requires the trigger to permit manual close; `GET /api/problems` carries
`manualClose` per problem so the UI never offers a Close that Zabbix will reject.

After a successful write nine cache prefixes are invalidated with a 15 s hold, and the change
is pushed immediately to every open SSE client.

Zabbix files every write under the write token's owner, so the portal user is put into the text:
the message Zabbix gets always starts with `[portal:<user>]`, also when the caller sent none.
Every attempt, refusal and failure is logged with the user, the address, the event ids and the
action. One request may name at most 50 event ids.

`message` is silently truncated at 2,048 characters, tag included. `acknowledge` defaults to true. Types
are checked, not coerced: a body that is not a JSON object, a `message` that is not text, or an
`acknowledge` or `close` that is not a boolean, such as the text `"false"`, is a 400.

eventids.description: One id or an array. Non-string members are dropped silently.

200.description: Written. `action` is the Zabbix bitmask, close 1, acknowledge 2, message 4.

400.description:
No usable event ids, more than 50 of them, a non-numeric id, a body or field of the wrong type, or nothing to do:
`acknowledge: false` with no `close` and no `message`.

403.description:
`forbidden`, the role is below operator, or `csrf`, a cookie request without
`X-HCML-CSRF: 1` or from another site (`CsrfRefused`).

503.description: `zabbix_write_disabled`, `ZABBIX_WRITE_TOKEN` is not set, or sign-in is off and `ALLOW_WRITE_WITHOUT_AUTH` is not true.

sessionCookie.name: hcml_session
sessionCookie.description:
The browser's scheme. The JWT in an httpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie, set by
`POST /api/auth/login` and `POST /api/auth/refresh` and cleared by `POST /api/auth/logout`.
Expires after `SESSION_HOURS` (12 hours by default), renewable while valid, carries
`{ sub, role, ep }`. The name is `SESSION_COOKIE`,
default `hcml_session`. Cookies ignore ports, so the Docker stack of hcml-portal-ollama
(port 8082) names it `hcml_session_ollama`, or signing in to one portal would replace the
other's session. Unsafe methods sent with this cookie need `X-HCML-CSRF: 1` (`CsrfHeader`).

bearerAuth.description:
The same JWT in an `Authorization` header, for scripts and tests: take it from the login
response's `Set-Cookie` header. Wins when a request carries the cookie too. Needs no
`X-HCML-CSRF` header, except on sign-in and sign-out, which always need it.

CsrfHeader.name: X-HCML-CSRF
CsrfHeader.description:
Must be `1` on sign-in, sign-out and every `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` or `DELETE` that
authenticates with the session cookie. A page on another site cannot add a custom header
without a CORS preflight, which the BFF answers only for `WEB_ORIGIN`. Not needed with a
Bearer header, except on sign-in and sign-out.

SetSessionCookie.description:
The session cookie, `hcml_session=<jwt>` with a `Max-Age` of the session length (43200 at the default
12 hours), `Path=/`, `HttpOnly` and
`SameSite=Strict`, plus `Secure` when the request arrived over HTTPS (`X-Forwarded-Proto: https`
behind a proxy trusted by `TRUST_PROXY`). The name follows `SESSION_COOKIE`.

BadRequest.description: `bad_request`, a query parameter or the request body failed validation.

Unauthorized.description: `unauthorized`, missing or expired portal JWT. Not the same as `zabbix_auth`.

Forbidden.description: `forbidden`, authenticated, but the role is below what this path requires.

CsrfRefused.description:
`csrf`, a possible cross-site forgery: an unsafe request sent with the session cookie, or a
sign-in or sign-out, without `X-HCML-CSRF: 1`, or with an `Origin` naming another site or
`null`. Answered before the guard, so it comes before any 401.

PayloadTooLarge.description: Body over Fastify's 1 MiB default, or over 4 KB on `POST /api/auth/login`.

RateLimited.description:
300 requests per minute per client, counted before the guard, so refused requests count too.
`/api/health`, `/api/stream` and `POST /api/auth/logout` are exempt. The stream has its own cap
instead, `429 too_many_streams`, described under `/api/stream`.

Internal.description: `internal`. The message is fixed; the detail is in the BFF log only.

ZabbixError.description: `zabbix_error`, unreachable, non-2xx, non-JSON-RPC, or a JSON-RPC error.

ZabbixUnavailable.description:
`zabbix_timeout` (no answer within `ZABBIX_TIMEOUT_MS`, default 10 s) or `zabbix_auth` (Zabbix
rejected the API token). Both are configuration states rather than upstream faults, which is
why they are 503 and not 504.

AiError.description:
`ai_error`, the model could not be reached, took too long, returned an error, answered
unusably or refused the portal's key (the sentence then says that trying again will not help). The message is one fixed sentence for the cause. The model's address and what it sent
back go to the BFF log only.

AiUnavailable.description:
`ai_disabled` (not configured) or `ai_busy` (the single concurrency slot is taken: carries
`Retry-After: 10`).

Error.description: The only error shape this server produces, at every status.

message.description: Safe to show a user. Never contains the Zabbix URL.

requestId.description: The reply's `X-Request-Id`. Quote it to an admin, who finds the request in the BFF log (`reqId`) and in nginx's (`rid=`).

ok.description: The portal can read Zabbix. The model never changes it.

zabbixMs.description: How long the Zabbix call took. Null when it did not answer.

model.description: `off` is no model configured, `not_checked` is the hosted Anthropic model, which a probe would bill.

checkedAt.description: When these answers were read, milliseconds since epoch.

build.description: The image's `BUILD_COMMIT` and `BUILD_TIME` build arguments. `unknown` when not given or empty, and cut to 64 characters.

Session.description: What sign-in and renewal return. The token is in the `Set-Cookie` header, never here.

expiresIn.description: Seconds the new session lasts: SESSION_HOURS times 3600, so 43200 (12 hours) by default.

SiteRef.description: A resolved site. No Zabbix entity corresponds to this.

HostState.description: The portal's reachability judgement, ping first.

StateReason.description: Which signal decided `HostState`. Provenance, so a wrong call can be traced.

maintenance_status.description: `1` while the host is in maintenance.

category.description: The monitoring template the kind was judged by, such as `Cisco IOS by SNMP`, `ICMP Ping` for a host that is only pinged, or `Other`.

value_type.description: `0` float, `1` character, `2` log, `3` unsigned integer, `4` text.

hosts.description: The host the item belongs to. Present when `itemids` is given, and always on the latest data.

manualClose.description: Whether the trigger permits manual close. Gates the Close button.

source.description: Which store answered. `trend+history` means trends stalled and raw filled the tail.

latestClock.description: The newest sample of any series, in epoch seconds. Null when no series has a sample.

downsampled.description: True when a series had more samples than `points` and was folded into equal time buckets.

host.description: The item's first host. An empty string when Zabbix names none.

units.description: An empty string when the item has none.

value_type.description: The Zabbix value type of the item, `0` float or `3` unsigned integer here.

delaySeconds.description:
Seconds between the item's values: its own interval, or for a dependent item the spacing
of its history, or `3600` with trends and `60` without when neither is known.

step.description: Render as a step line, ICMP and other 0/1 series.

stats.description: Over the samples the series holds. Null when it holds none.

lastClock.description: Epoch seconds of the newest sample.

coverage.description: How much of the window the samples cover. The two clocks are epoch seconds, null with no sample.

GraphPoint.description:
`[ms, avg, min, max]`: the time in epoch milliseconds, then the average, the minimum and the
maximum. A null `avg` is an explicit collection gap. `min` and `max` are null for raw history.

icmp.description: Null when the host has no ICMP items. `up`, `loss` and `latency` are there only when a fresh value exists.

considered.description: Hosts that have such an item.

current.description: Of those, with a current value.

clock.description: When the value was collected, epoch seconds.

total.description: Enabled scenarios on monitored hosts. It is `ok`, `failed` and `unknown` added up.

step.description: The step that failed, counting from 1.

clock.description: When the result was collected, epoch seconds.

from.description: Where the zone starts, in the item's units. It ends where the next one starts, or at the top of the scale.

level.description: What the zone's colour in Zabbix means (red is `critical`, orange and yellow `warn`, green `ok`, blue `low`, grey or unset `none`).

direction.description: The opposite of the gauge's own direction.

value.description: The item's current value. Null when it has none: it is never read from history.

id.description: Stable for one item (`item-<id>`); a widget without an item is named after its title.

title.description: The widget's own title, as HCML wrote it.

page.description: The dashboard page the widget sits on.

hostid.description: The host's id in Zabbix, which the Graphs page needs.

item.description: The item's name, such as "Interface wan1(): Bits received".

link.description:
What the interface says about itself, from its status item (IF-MIB ifOperStatus) when that has a
current value. `down` is 2 (down) or 7 (lowerLayerDown): a link that carries nothing, so a reading
of 0 is not an idle link. `up` is 1. `unknown` is no current status, or one that is neither
working nor dead (testing, dormant, not present).

other.description: The opposite direction of the same interface, on the gauge's own scale and zones. Null for a gauge with no direction, or with no item of the opposite direction.

units.description: The item's units; every number below is in them.

clock.description: When the value was collected, epoch seconds.

max.description: The top of the scale, the link's capacity as the widget gives it.

state.description:
`ok` a current reading. `stale` an old one (value and time are given). `nodata` the item has
never held a value this portal can read. `unsupported` the item is disabled or Zabbix cannot
collect it. `missing` the widget points at an item that is gone. `invalid` the widget has no
usable scale (the value is still given).

dashboard.description: The dashboard that was looked for.

critical.description: Of those, in a red zone.

warn.description: Of those, in a yellow or orange zone.

unavailable.description: No gauge to draw: no value, unsupported, missing, or a scale that cannot be read.

down.description: Links whose interface is down, whatever their reading says.

otherHigh.description: Links whose opposite direction is in a yellow, orange or red zone now.

InterfaceRow.description: One interface, with the `net.if.*` items Zabbix discovers for its SNMP index folded together.

speed.description: Null when no speed is reported or it is zero.

utilisation.description: Percent of `speed` the busier direction uses, to two decimals. Null without a speed or a reading.

lastclock.description: Epoch seconds of the newest fresh value of any of its items. Null when none is fresh.

itemids.description: The item behind each figure, for a link to its graph.

coverage.description: How many hosts each site signal accounted for. The standardisation metric.

available.description: By interface flags, as before `state` existed.

up.description: By derived `state`. Disabled hosts count only in `disabled`.

worst.description: Highest severity firing here; -1 when clear.
Worst status anywhere; -1 when everything is fine.

ServiceNode.description: Recursive, depth-capped at 12. De-duplicated by `serviceid`, the graph is a DAG.

status.description: -1 is OK; otherwise the severity that propagated up.

errorBudget.description: Seconds still absorbable; negative means missed.

noDataWindows.description: Spans declared not measured (SLA_NO_DATA_WINDOWS), treated as hours with no data.

DerivedServiceNode.description: A `ServiceNode` of the tree derived from the estate, whose children are of the same kind.

slo.description: The promised availability target in percent, such as `99.9`.

error_budget.description: Seconds left before the SLO is missed.

end.description: `min(to, now)`, the part of the window that has happened.

basis.description: What the figure counts, so two profiles can be compared like for like.

maintenancePolicy.description:
Time inside a planned Zabbix maintenance window counts neither as down nor in the
total, in both profiles. Read from the periods as Zabbix defines them now.

gaps.description: Estate-wide spans in which almost nothing was collected.

noDataWindows.description:
Spans the setting SLA_NO_DATA_WINDOWS declares not measured, such as a collector that ran outside
HCML's network. Both methods treat them as hours with no data.

stats.description:
`zabbixCalls` under-counts: sliced `event.get` recursion is counted once, so the true
figure is higher whenever a window exceeds 5,000 events.

SliGroup.description: One roll-up row, for the whole estate or for one category, site or kind of device.

withData.description: Hosts with enough collected data to have a figure.

sli.description: Percent. The plain mean of the figures of the hosts that have one, HCML's own rule for every total. Null when none has.

meeting.description: Whether `sli` reaches the target. Null when there is no figure.

belowTarget.description: Hosts whose own figure is below the target.

SliHost.description: One device in the derived monthly report.

hostStatus.description: The Zabbix host status, `0` monitored and `1` not.

category.description: The monitoring template the kind was judged by, or `Other`.

deviceClass.description: The kind of device, as `class` on `/api/devices`.

triggerids.description: The trigger ids the figure is read from.

sli.description: Percent. Null when too little data was collected to say.

downtime.description: Seconds down inside the measured time.

window.description: Seconds in the window, from its start to now or to its end.

covered.description: Seconds actually measured: the window minus hours with no data and planned maintenance.

maintenance.description: Seconds of the window inside planned maintenance, left out of the figure.

coverage.description: The share of the measurable time that was measured, 0 to 1.

measured.description:
False when the ICMP of this host has never been collected. HCML's method still counts such a
host as 100 percent. The figures do not change, this only says so.

errorBudget.description: Seconds of downtime the target still allows. Negative when missed.

SliPath.description: A redundant pair of WAN links. It is down only while every leg is down.

SliWeb.description: One web scenario in the derived monthly report.

HostAvailability.description: One host of the availability report.

availability.description: Percent of the measured time with no qualifying problem open. Null means no data.

downtime.description: Seconds spent in a problem state, with overlaps merged.

coverage.description: The share of the measurable time that was measured, 0 to 1. Only with `basis=availability`.

AvailabilityReport.description:
`overall`, `categories`, `sites`, `target`, `profile` and `gaps` are present only when
`basis=availability`. `truncated` is always false with `basis=availability`. With `basis=all-problems`
it is true only when more than 200 outages from before the look-back needed a one-by-one lookup
and the rest were left out, so the figures are a floor. Events are sliced, never silently cut.

noDataWindows.description: Spans declared not measured (SLA_NO_DATA_WINDOWS), in which no downtime is counted.

concentration.description: The Pareto line: N triggers produced X percent of all alerts.

total.description: Triggers before `top` cut the list. Aggregates cover all.

count.description: How many times it fired in the window.

medianDuration.description: Seconds. The median, so that one long outlier does not hide many short firings.

shortLived.description: Firings that cleared before anyone could realistically act.

ackRate.description: 0 to 1. Zero across many firings means the team has learned to ignore it.

unacknowledged.description: Open problems nobody has acknowledged. The buckets count these.

oldest.description: The unacknowledged problems that have waited longest, at most 20, oldest first.

host.description: An empty string when the problem has no host.

clock.description: Epoch seconds the problem began, as Zabbix writes it.

key.description: In practice `cpu`, `memory`, `disk` or `ifutil`; typed open server-side.

avg.description: Unweighted mean of the hourly averages.

hint.description: Interpolated from env, so not an enumerable constant.

scored.description: False when this deployment has not configured the check.

MapDetail.description: A Zabbix map as `map.get` returns it, with its elements and links.

label.description: As written in Zabbix, with its macros.

elementtype.description: `0` host, `1` map, `2` trigger, `3` host group, `4` image.

labelText.description: The label with the host macros expanded.

problems.description: Host elements only. Open problems of the host.

maxSeverity.description: Host elements only. The worst open severity, -1 when there is none.

color.description: Hex without the `#`, as Zabbix stores it.

noData.description: True when there was nothing to measure, so no model call was made.
